candidate.answerReason: The first three-digit multiple is 13 × 8 = 104 and the last is 13 × 76 = 988. The integer multipliers from 8 through 76 number 69.

methods.label: Count the eligible multipliers
methods.explanation:
Every positive number divisible by \(13\) can be written as \(13k\), where \(k\) is a positive integer. Finding the first and last eligible multipliers lets us count all the numbers without listing them.

At the lower end,
\[
13\cdot7=91,\qquad 13\cdot8=104,
\]
so \(8\) is the first multiplier producing a three-digit number. At the upper end,
\[
13\cdot76=988,\qquad 13\cdot77=1001,
\]
so \(76\) is the last.

Every integer multiplier from \(8\) through \(76\) produces a different three-digit multiple, and every three-digit multiple occurs this way. Including both endpoints, the count is
\[
76-8+1=\boxed{69},
\]
choice C.
methods.levelReason: Adjacent multiples establish the endpoints, followed by elementary inclusive counting.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task is to find and count all integer multipliers in a bounded range, fitting cnm_h020. Factors and multiples supply the interpretation of divisibility. The endpoint products establish the range directly, without requiring a general inequality-solving procedure.

review.mathematicalCheck: The adjacent products 91 and 104 establish multiplier 8 as the first eligible value; 988 and 1001 establish 76 as the last. Multipliers 8 through 76 correspond uniquely to all three-digit multiples, giving 76 − 8 + 1 = 69.
